1.why: Verify uses the session-bound recovery token and reset-password further requires state.recovery.accountRef === "protected-account".

2.why: Recovery state lives only on the requesting session; another session has no matching recovery token so the same code fails verification.

3.why: Password reset only clears resetAuthorized/mfaPending on the current session and never deletes or de-authenticates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is TLS-only with HTTPS enforcement and HSTS, but no explicit minimum TLS version is configured in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and session state are stored in memory as plaintext, not encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent; API messages are generic, yet the mock delivery path returns the raw token and link in the JSON body.

7.why: Identifiers are regex-validated, passwords policy-checked, comparisons are length-safe, and the client inserts values only via textContent.

8.why: Navigation is same-origin history.pushState/safeView allowlist; mockRecoveryLink is only "/?view=verify&token=..." on this host.

9.why: There are no email templates rendering user input; nothing injects user-controlled HTML or scripts into messages.

10.why: The SPA log panel and console explicitly print mockDeliveryToken, mock recovery links, and mockMfaCode.

11.why: Password hashes use bcrypt in memory, but MFA_TEST_CODE and the mock recovery identifier are hardcoded secrets in source.

12.why: No default account password is defined, but the fixed MFA_TEST_CODE "246810" acts as a built-in default verification secret.

13.why: tokenAttempts and mfaAttempts lock out after MAX_FAILURES (5) for BLOCK_MS (60s) with 429 responses.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same generic ok message; existence is only hinted when mockDeliveryToken is added for the demo identifier.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), are single-use/expiring, and stored per session with accountRef.
